recordedAtUtcSource: date -u, read from the shell at write time
whatThisRecordIs: a READ-ONLY provenance supplement. It adds a full 64-hex run reference to CURRENT terminal acquisition episodes whose authoritative A2 source record published only a 16-hex prefix
whatThisRecordIsNot: an A3 record, registry entry or parser
networkUsed: none. No institution request of any kind was issued
databaseWrittenByThisRecord: none. Every statement was a SELECT executed as the readonly role

canonicalStart.whatTheOneExtraCommitContains: PHASE_2B_2D_A2_POST_SD9_RECONCILIATION_RESERVE_SCARCITY_AND_ACQUISITION_RESUME_V1.json - the post-reconciliation owner decisions and a 4-window / 20-attempt bounded acquisition authority, recorded under the immediately preceding owner task and pushed before this task was issued
canonicalStart.whyItDoesNotContaminateThisClosure: that authority is UNUSED. No window was planned, no reserve was assigned, no ledger append was made, no network request was issued and no database row was written. This task is read-only and its inputs are the frozen draw, the committed 30-entry ledger, committed A2 governance bytes and read-only database metadata - none of which that commit touches
canonicalStart.ownerDecisionStillNeeded: whether that bounded acquisition authority stands unused or is withdrawn. This closure neither consumes nor cancels it

a3ConsumerContractReadOnly.predicateLocation: families.ts:37 (LOWER_HEX_SHA256), enforced by the hex() guard at families.ts:154
a3ConsumerContractReadOnly.r17StatedRunRefSemantics: R17 section 15 says READY carries runRefSha256 'exactly as the public records bind it (SHA-256 of the database run id)' and that R18 may prove sha256(databaseRunId) === runRefSha256

theProvenanceDefect.symptom: historical A2 acquisition records did not all publish the same run-reference shape. Later records publish runRefSha256 as a full lower-hex SHA-256; five earlier window families publish only runRefSha256Prefix with 16 hex characters
theProvenanceDefect.whyThatWasSufficientThen: A2's own adjudication resolved the prefix uniquely against the working database at the time
theProvenanceDefect.whyItIsNotSufficientNow: A3 committed-governance authority requires a full SHA-256-shaped run binding and performs no database lookup
theProvenanceDefect.howItWasClosed: upstream, in A2, append-only, by mechanical resolution - never by inferring or padding the missing characters

twoHistoricalRunReferenceConventionsExis.finding: the A2 corpus contains TWO run-reference derivations, and they are not interchangeable. This record does not normalise them

conventionOne.derivation: sha256(UTF-8 bytes of 'run:' + the lowercase canonical 8-4-4-4-12 run UUID)
conventionOne.usedBy: the five prefix-publishing window families closed here

conventionTwo.derivation: sha256(UTF-8 bytes of the lowercase canonical 8-4-4-4-12 run UUID), with NO prefix
conventionTwo.usedBy: the Generation-1 SD9 reconciliation at d6f783c, the Batch-01 per-slot attribution adjudication, and the later full-runRefSha256 window families

twoHistoricalRunReferenceConventionsExis.theProofThatBothNameTheSameRun: selection index 59's run is published twice in committed A2 governance: the Window-D1 adjudication carries the prefix a76be03c901fda20, which completes under convention one to a76be03c901fda20dba06ffe269a5c615f6acbcaa6c5fce9abdb5747183b1141, and the reconciliation publishes fbb6bfda139f3fef7527df21cce4549bed8b0bcb15d6b8fcfe90ddb28456df1d for the same run under convention two. Both were recomputed here from the same database run id
twoHistoricalRunReferenceConventionsExis.consequenceA3MustHandle: R17 section 15 anticipates convention two (sha256(databaseRunId)). Every runRefSha256 this closure emits is convention ONE, because it must complete a committed 16-hex prefix and convention two does not. An R18 check written as sha256(runId) === runRefSha256 would REFUSE all thirteen. Each entry therefore also carries the same run's convention-two digest, explicitly labelled, so A3 can reconcile the corpus without this record choosing for it

fiveFurtherSlotsAlreadyCarryBothConventi.situation: each of these five publishes a convention-one 16-hex PREFIX in its own window adjudication and a convention-two FULL digest in the reconciliation. They are therefore already class A (a full run reference is committed) but under the OTHER convention from their own adjudication. No closure entry is emitted for them; they are recorded here so the mixed-convention corpus is visible to A3 rather than discovered by it

census.method: for every selection index 0..109 the CURRENT occupant was derived with the landed currentOccupantForSelectionIndex over the frozen draw plus the committed 30-entry ledger; the occupant was then looked up in the database by eche_row_key; its acquisition-of-record run is its LATEST run by orgunit_research_runs.started_at; both convention digests were computed for that run and searched, as full 64-hex and as 16-hex prefixes, across every committed JSON file in docs/evaluation
census.supersededHistoricalOccupantsWereNotClos: a historical failed occupant whose slot is now held by a later reserve is audit history, not current authority. No closure entry was created for one

a3Handoff.thisRecordSupplies: full run-reference bindings that were missing from thirteen older A2 window adjudications, each bound to the exact source adjudication and LIVE_RESULT that remains its disposition authority
a3Handoff.a3MustBindBoth: the historical terminal fact AND this closure entry. A closure entry alone carries no disposition and must never be read as one
a3Handoff.a3MustDecideTheConventionQuestion: two run-reference derivations exist in the corpus. This record publishes both digests per entry, labelled, and designates neither. How R32 / Governance V4 verifies a run reference is an A3 decision
